title: Etale/pro-etale comparison normalized on scalar Kummer classes and mates
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, $N\geq1$, $r=\ell^N$, and $A$ a finite free commutative $\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z$-algebra. For each $k$-scheme $T$, put $L_T^e=\mu_{r,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/r}A_T$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. Use the comparison $C_T=\nu_T^*$ from etale to pro-etale module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and put $L_T^p=C_TL_T^e$. Identify the roots, tensor twists and coefficient maps by the canonical comparison used in [def-pur-affine-line-datum]. For any unit $w$ on $T$, write $\kappa_T^e(w)=H^1(z\mapsto z\otimes1_A)(\delta_T(w))$, with $\delta_T$ the ordinary $r$-Kummer boundary [def-sc-kummer-sequence]. Define $\kappa_T^p(w)$ as the image of this class under the canonical abelian cohomology pullback of [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison]. These definitions apply to arbitrary $k$-schemes, not just finite-type schemes.

Let $c^q_{T,L^e}:H^q(T_{\mathrm{et}},L_T^e)\to H^q(T_{\mathrm{proet}},L_T^p)$ be the module comparison induced by the derived comparison unit followed by the canonical final-object direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology]. After the canonical scalar-forgetting identifications, $c^q_{T,L^e}$ is exactly the abelian canonical cohomology pullback for every $q\geq0$. In particular
$$c^1_{T,L^e}(\kappa_T^e(w))=\kappa_T^p(w).$$

For a qcqs $k$-morphism $a:X\to B$ and $F\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, let $b_{a,F}:C_BRa_{\mathrm{et},*}F\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{\mathrm{proet},*}C_XF$ be the canonical invertible counit-mate comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. For every $M\in D^+(B_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, it satisfies $b_{a,a^*M}\circ C_B(\eta_a^e(M))=\eta_a^p(C_BM)$ after identifying $C_Xa^*M$ with $a_{\mathrm{proet}}^*C_BM$ through the specified inverse-image comparison. For $F=L_X^e$, its first cohomology sends the comparison pullback of the edge section of $\kappa_X^e(w)$ to the edge section of $\kappa_X^p(w)$. More generally it carries cohomology sheaves through the exact functor $C_B$, and hence preserves the invertibility of the normalized unit and edge-generator maps and the asserted vanishings whenever these have been established on the etale site.

For every cartesian square $(a,a',g,v)$ with $a$ and $a'$ qcqs, its specified pullback/direct-image comparisons $S:C_{B'}g^*Ra_*\xrightarrow{\sim}g_{\mathrm{proet}}^*Ra_{\mathrm{proet},*}C_X$ and $T:C_{B'}Ra'_*v^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra'_{\mathrm{proet},*}v_{\mathrm{proet}}^*C_X$ satisfy
$$T\circ C_{B'}(\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathrm{et}})=\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathrm{proet}}\circ S,$$ where $\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathrm{et}}:g^*Ra_*\to Ra'_*v^*$ is the etale derived exchange [sbc-def-base-change-map] and $\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathrm{proet}}:g_{\mathrm{proet}}^*Ra_{\mathrm{proet},*}\to Ra'_{\mathrm{proet},*}v_{\mathrm{proet}}^*$ is the ambient constant-ring pro-etale exchange [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange].
Thus invertibility of etale exchange implies invertibility of the specified pro-etale exchange. For every $k$-morphism $u:T'\to T$, the canonical pro-etale pullback satisfies $u^*\kappa_T^p(w)=\kappa_{T'}^p(u^*w)$ through the specified coefficient identifications. These assertions hold for $g:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$ even if $\Omega$ is not finite type over $k$. In the purity datum, $L_T^p=A(1)_T$ under its specified identification, so the class in the displayed equality is the datum's actual $\kappa(t)$ when $T=\mathbf G_{m,B}$ and $w=t$.

proof.text: For each $T$, apply [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] at the terminal objects of its two small sites, to the constant ring $A$. Its normalized comparisons commute with canonical global-cohomology pullback. The exact module lift of $\nu_T^{-1}$ has the underlying abelian inverse image and the same forgotten unit by [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. The map $c^q_{T,L^e}$ is precisely this module pullback: [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology] specifies it as the derived unit followed by terminal direct-image evaluation. Consequently, writing $j_e,j_p$ for the scalar-forgetting identifications, the cited pullback compatibility gives $j_p c^q_{T,L^e}=\nu_T^*j_e$, with the specified coefficient identification on the target. This is an equality of the named maps in every $q\geq0$, not just an isomorphism of their groups. The abelian comparison is invertible by [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison]. None of these inputs assumes that $T$ is finite type.

source.place: Opening paragraph, comparison of the classes: scalar-forgetting normalization; Stacks 03FD, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, and 099W, proetale.tex, lemma-compare-cohomology.

proof.text: Since $r$ is invertible on every $k$-scheme, [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] gives the ordinary exact Kummer sequence on each $T$. For $u:T'\to T$, pullback of local units defines $d:u^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,T}\to\mathbf G_{m,T'}$; $d(z^r)=d(z)^r$, so it restricts to the root comparison and gives a morphism of these exact sequences. These are the specified root identifications: choose a primitive root $\zeta\in k$ by [lem-sc-primitive-root] and factor $x^r-1=\prod_{i=0}^{r-1}(x-\zeta^i)$. Distinct factors differ by units, so roots on any $k$-scheme are locally uniquely $\zeta^i$. Pullback preserves the exponent; thus $u^{-1}\mu_{r,T}\cong\mu_{r,T'}$ is the identity on these locally constant exponents. Tensor coordinates send $\zeta^i\otimes a$ to $ia$, and identify $u^{-1}(z\mapsto z\otimes1_A)$ with the same map on $T'$. Coefficient naturality is [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback](2); compatibility with the derived Kummer boundary is [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder](3). The resolution and derived-triangle connecting conventions agree by [lem-sc-p1-right-derived-triangle-connecting]. Naturality of connecting maps for the displayed morphism of exact sequences is [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor]. Hence $u^*\kappa_T^e(w)=\kappa_{T'}^e(u^*w)$. This uses no module structure on $\mathbf G_m$.

source.place: Opening paragraph and Step 3, pullback of the ordinary Kummer boundary before extending its roots-of-unity coefficient; Stacks sites-cohomology.tex, cohomological pullback and connecting maps.

proof.text:
By definition $\kappa_T^p(w)=
u_T^*(H^1(z\mapsto z\otimes1_A)\delta_T(w))$. Substitute this expression in Step 1 to get $c^1_{T,L^e}(\kappa_T^e(w))=\kappa_T^p(w)$. For $u:T'	o T$, the two composites of geometric inverse images around the comparison square are canonically identified, compatibly with composition, by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The composition and coefficient-naturality laws of [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback](2),(4) therefore give $u_p^*
u_T^*\kappa_T^e(w)=
u_{T'}^*u_e^*\kappa_T^e(w)$. Step 2 makes this $\kappa_{T'}^p(u^*w)$. In the purity datum the final paragraph of [def-pur-affine-line-datum] defines its class by this very abelian comparison of the same etale boundary and coefficient morphism. Under its specified twist identification our formula for $T=\mathbf G_{m,B}$ and $w=t$ is therefore its actual $\kappa(t)$.

source.place: Opening paragraph, actual scalar Kummer class, and Step 3, pullback of the coordinate class.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] for the qcqs morphism $a$. Put $l=a_e^*$, $p=a_p^*$ and let $\alpha:C_Xl\cong pC_B$ be the specified inverse-image comparison. The cited theorem defines $b$ as the right mate of $\alpha^{-1}$ and proves it invertible, with its counit equation. Apply [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility] with $L_1=l$, $L_2=p$, $G=C_B$, $H=C_X$ and transformation $\alpha^{-1}:pC_B\to C_Xl$. It gives $b_{a,lM}\,C_B(\eta_a^e(M))=Ra_{p,*}(\alpha_M^{-1})\,\eta_a^p(C_BM)$. Identifying $C_XlM$ with $pC_BM$ by $\alpha_M$ yields exactly the unit equation in the statement. Thus the assertion holds for every bounded-below $M$, not only for constants.

source.place: Opening paragraph, transport of units by the canonical counit mate; Stacks 0B65, categories.tex, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-site-comparison-edge-section] with $\Lambda=A$, $u=a$, $F=L_X^e$, $q=1$ and $x=\kappa_X^e(w)$. It states exactly $e_p(c^1x)=\Gamma(\mathcal H^1b)(C_B(e_e(x)))$. Step 3 identifies $c^1x$ with $\kappa_X^p(w)$, proving the required edge-section equality. By [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact](3), $\mathcal H^q(C_BK)\cong C_B\mathcal H^q(K)$ naturally in $K$; composing with $\mathcal H^q(b)$ identifies $C_BR^qa_{e,*}F$ with $R^qa_{p,*}C_XF$. Exactness carries a zero sheaf to zero. Functors carry inverse pairs to inverse pairs, so an invertible etale unit or generator map remains invertible after $C_B$ and these comparison isomorphisms. The unit and edge equations just proved identify these transported arrows with the normalized pro-etale arrows. For the generator map, $A$-linearity means that the image of $1$ determines the map from $A_B$, so equality of the edge sections is sufficient.

source.place: Opening paragraph, transport of edge generators and vanishings; Stacks 072W, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-higher-direct-images, and 099W, proetale.tex, lemma-compare-cohomology.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-discrete-exchange-site-comparison] with $\Lambda=A$, $f=a$, $f'=a'$, $g$ and $g'=v$; its hypotheses are the cartesian square and qcqs $f,f'$ only. Its $b_f,b_{f'}$ are normalized as the adjoint transposes of $A_U(\varepsilon^e_u)\circ a_{u,r_u}^{-1}$, which is exactly the canonical mate of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] used in the statement, and its $a_u$ are the canonical inverse-image comparisons. Hence its $S_L=p_g(b_{f,L})\circ a_{g,r_fL}$ and $T_L=s_{f'}(a_{g',L})\circ b_{f',l_{g'}L}$ are the statement's $S$ and $T$. Its etale exchange is the module exchange of [sk-def-exchange], the $D^+$ restriction of the unbounded mate of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]; [sbc-def-base-change-map] identifies $\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathrm{et}}$ with that same mate on the exchanged square, so the two agree. Its pro-etale exchange is precisely $\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathrm{proet}}$ of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] with the constant coefficient rings. The cited equality is therefore $T\,C_{B'}(\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathrm{et}})=\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathrm{proet}}\,S$ in the statement's orientation. $S$ and $T$ are invertible, since $a,a'$ are qcqs. If $\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathrm{et}}$ is invertible, then $\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathrm{proet}}=T\,C_{B'}(\operatorname{Ex}_{\mathrm{et}})\,S^{-1}$ is an invertible composite. The cited theorem puts no qcqs or finite-type condition on $g$ or $v$, and Steps 1–5 use none either. So the argument applies to $g:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$ for every algebraically closed extension field $\Omega$, as asserted.
